newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Crean in final stage of talks on disposals.
newsitem.headline: Crean in final stage of talks on disposals.

text.p: Irish-based industrial holding group James Crean Plc said on Tuesday that it is in the final stages of negotiation in relation to a number of disposals as part of a restructuring of the group.

"While it is not possible to comment on these negotiations at this time because of commercial sensitivity, announcements will be made as the restructuring process is completed," the company said in its annual results statement.

Crean, which bought out the minority shareholdings in associate Inishtech last year, said at the time that it would sell Inishtech, an industrial holding group with interests in printing and packaging, to a third party.

As part of its restructuring, Crean said it intended to offer to redeem 32.2 million Irish pounds of convertible loan stock outstanding at par together with a sum equal to the accrued interest at the date of redemption.

"Following the restructuring, borrowings will be sharply reduced and the group will have the financial and management resources necessary to sustain a programme of expansion within the retained businesses.
"The result will be a slimmed down, re-shaped and more focused Crean with attractive growth opportunities," the company said.
Crean's debt/equity ratio stood at 85 percent at year-end if the convertible loan stock is included.
